definitions.explanation: To become elderly or advanced in years. Often used for people and animals.
Figuratively, when something loses its vitality or freshness.

examples.english: My parents have also grown old.

examples.japanese: {老|お}いて⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{元気|げんき}→元気：00696_genki⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦いたい→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: I want to stay healthy even when I grow old.

examples.japanese: {老|お}いた⟦{犬|いぬ}→犬：00632_inu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{日向|ひなた}ぼっこ→日向ぼっこ：18018_hinatabokko⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦している→する：00392_suru⟧。
⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{誰|だれ}でも→誰でも：08498_daredemo⟧{老|お}いて⟦いく→行く：00119_iku⟧。
⟦{祖母|そぼ}→祖母：00813_sobo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{老|お}いて⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦なお→なお：00305_nao⟧、⟦{毎日|まいにち}→毎日：00729_mainichi⟧⟦{散歩|さんぽ}→散歩：02885_sanpo⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{続|つづ}けている→続ける：01231_tsuzukeru⟧。
examples.english: Even in her old age, my grandmother continues her daily walks.

examples.japanese: ⟦{建物|たてもの}→建物：01458_tatemono⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{老|お}いて、⟦あちこち→あちこち：01687_achikochi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{傷|いた}み→痛み：01795_itami⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{見|み}える→見える：01165_mieru⟧。
examples.english: The building has aged, and damage can be seen here and there.

examples.japanese: {老|お}いた⟦{町|まち}→町：00613_machi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{新|あたら}しい→新しい：00506_atarashii⟧⟦{風|かぜ}→風：00641_kaze⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{吹|ふ}き{込|こ}みたい→吹き込む：11962_fukikomu⟧。
examples.english: I want to breathe new life into this aging town.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{会社|かいしゃ}→会社：00607_kaisha⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{組織|そしき}→組織：03320_soshiki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{老|お}いて⟦きている→来る：00254_kuru⟧。
examples.english: This company's organization is becoming worn and outdated.

examples.japanese: ⟦{文化|ぶんか}→文化：01504_bunka⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{老|お}いて、⟦{新|あたら}しい→新しい：00506_atarashii⟧⟦もの→物：02259_mono⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{生|う}まれ→生まれる：00905_umareru⟧⟦なくなった→無くなる：01101_nakunaru⟧。
examples.english: The culture has grown stale and stopped producing anything new.

notes:
{老|お}いる is an intransitive verb (⟦{自動詞|じどうし}→自動詞：10977_jidoushi⟧). It is classified as an ichidan verb but has some irregular features from classical Japanese. There is no transitive pair.

ASPECT (ている):
{老|お}いている indicates an ongoing or resulting state of being old.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {老|お}いて⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦なお→なお：00305_nao⟧ - even in old age
- {老|お}いた⟦{親|おや}→親：01357_oya⟧ - aged parents
- ⟦{年|とし}→年：00486_toshi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}って→取る：00565_toru⟧{老|お}いる - to grow old with age

LITERARY NOTE:
This verb has a somewhat literary or formal feel. In everyday speech, ⟦{年|とし}→年：00486_toshi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}る→取る：00565_toru⟧ is more commonly used to express aging.
